title: Shin Mina reflects on The Remarried Empress and its global success
body_md:
Ahead of the final two episodes of The Remarried Empress, Shin Mina has discussed the experience of portraying Empress Navier, the challenges of adapting a popular webtoon and the unexpectedly international response to the Korean fantasy romance.

The series premiered on November 3, 2026, and reportedly became the most-viewed local original premiere globally on Disney+ within three days. Worldwide premiere views subsequently increased by approximately 40 percent between the first and second weeks. Latin America recorded growth of 43 percent, while the Asia-Pacific and Europe, Middle East and Africa regions each grew by 39 percent. The United States registered an increase of 37 percent.

Adapted from a Naver webtoon, the drama follows Navier as her marriage and position at court come under pressure. The story combines palace politics and fantastical elements with a romance centered on a woman who seeks to determine the terms of her own future.

Shin was particularly attracted to the character's dignity, wisdom and inner strength. Although the actress has previously appeared in fantasy-inflected historical television, playing an empress in an invented society with its own hierarchy presented a different opportunity. She also recognized emotional connections between Navier's journey and characters from her earlier romantic projects.

The production distinguishes itself from many Korean period dramas through European-inspired costumes and locations. Filming took place in castles and palaces in Germany and the Czech Republic. Shin explained that the elaborate wardrobe and unfamiliar historical settings helped her immerse herself in the fictional world, even when some costumes were physically uncomfortable.

The actress also acknowledged the pressure that accompanies adapting a story with an established international readership. Fans already have their own impressions of the characters, and a live-action interpretation must establish an identity without losing the qualities that attracted readers in the first place.

The ensemble includes Ju Jihoon, Lee Jongsuk and Lee Seyoung. Cho Suwon directed the series, which was produced by Studio N and adapted by Yeoh Geena and Hyun Choongyeol.

The final two episodes arrive on Disney+ and Hulu on November 25, 2026. Despite the strong reception, the producers have not announced a second season. Audience enthusiasm therefore should not be confused with an official renewal.

The show's reported performance offers an interesting example of how webtoon adaptations can travel beyond their domestic market. Its combination of recognizable emotional conflicts, a distinctive fantasy setting and ambitious production design has helped create an identity that does not depend exclusively on familiarity with Korean historical drama.

Would you prefer to see Navier's story continue in a second season, or would a satisfying conclusion be enough?
